newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WOODSIDE SIGNS NEW AUSTRALIA GAS DEAL.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WOODSIDE SIGNS NEW AUSTRALIA GAS DEAL.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd, operator of the North West Shelf oil and gas project off Western Australia, said on Wednesday it had signed a new 15-year contract to supply Western Australian government-owned Alinta Gas.
Alinta Gas has agreed to buy up to 80 terrajoules of natural gas a day from the North-West Shelf domestic joint venture at Karratha under the new contract, which begins in 2005.
Woodside managing director John Akehurst said in a statement the new deal took their association with Alinta Gas well beyond the expiry date of existing contracts.
The extension of the gas contract to 2020 would allow Alinta Gas to offer long-term competitive prices to domestic and industrial gas consumers in Western Australia, he said.
Existing contracts to supply Alinta Gas were due to expire on June 30 2005, a company spokesman said.
Woodside has a 50 percent share of the North-West Shelf Domestic Gas Joint Venture, while subsidiaries of The British Petroleum Co Ltd and Chevron Inc both hold 16 and two-third percent stakes.
Subsidiaries of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Royal Dutch/Shell Group both hold eight and one-third percent interests.
